app.title: Field specific lacuna identifier: literature discovery, thesis gap finding and topic mapping
app.summary: A person writes a research specification as concept groups with synonyms, year and type limits and sources. They can fill a form or paste and validate a JSON request, and can upload their own PDFs and record files. A run collects publication records from bibliographic sources within fixed request limits and ranks them by how close their text is to the specification. The person filters the ranked table and opens each record to read its evidence excerpts and page positions. In separate modes they can pull the limitations and future-work statements that thesis authors wrote about a topic, or place a topic in a research taxonomy. Finally they export a single self-contained brief, or technical packages, for their own assistant to interpret.

task.text: Find the published work closest to a planned study, or the gaps that thesis authors reported in a field, and hand the evidence on as a self-contained brief.

data.text: Bibliographic records retrieved from scholarly indexes or imported from files, with abstracts and, where it can be read, PDF full text split into physical pages; also extracted quoted passages and a topic taxonomy.
data.item: a publication record (title, abstract, year, type, DOI) with optional full-text pages and evidence excerpts

stage.text: scoping prior literature and open problems before proposing a study

mechanism.text: A specification form or JSON editor drives a bounded retrieval run. The results then appear in tabs: a ranked table with a selector that opens one record's evidence, a table of gap candidates with their quoted sources, and a taxonomy tree drawn for a chosen placement. An artifacts tab turns the active run, or one reloaded from the local run store, into a downloadable brief.

field.text: literature search and research-gap identification using lexical retrieval over scholarly indexes

workflow.name: gather and rank sources against a specification, inspect their evidence, and export a brief

steps.here: Fill the specification form (concept groups with synonyms separated by |, mechanism groups, seed titles, years, publication types, sources and limits) or paste or upload a request JSON and validate it against the schema. Optional PDF and CSV/JSON record uploads are added. A saved run can be reloaded from the local run store instead.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run discovery queries OpenAlex, Crossref, CORE or OAI-PMH within the per-source, query and request budgets, removes duplicate records, and scores each record by proximity = 0.70 word + 0.30 character TF-IDF cosine × 100.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A score-first table can be narrowed by a title/DOI substring and a minimum score. Each row shows how many concept groups matched and the evidence level (full text, abstract or title).

A study selector opens the record's authors, source link, word and character scores, concept and mechanism matches, and evidence excerpts with matched terms and physical PDF page. Possible duplicates are flagged for review.

steps.step: pull marked statements out of the texts and group them
steps.here: Field gaps mode takes a topic and retrieves theses only. Cue rules extract limitation, future-work and open-question quotes with offsets and pages, and identical wording is grouped. Each candidate then shows its sources and the result of a bounded follow-up search for later related work.

steps.step: place the topic in a hierarchy
steps.here: Topic branches mode samples publications to suggest domain → field → subfield → topic placements, with neighbouring topics. The person chooses one placement to draw as a tree and can also read it as a text tree.

A concise or extended assistant brief (.md) can be downloaded, copied, or saved to a folder without overwriting earlier briefs. Optional full or compact ZIP packages and the result JSON are available, along with gap JSON/Markdown and branch SVG/JSON/Markdown.

distinctive: The proximity score is lexical and labelled throughout as uncalibrated, not a novelty probability, and no language model is ever called.
Every run is bounded by explicit request budgets and page and download caps, and coverage, source failures and unread pages are kept visible.

Gap candidates are author-reported and always marked unverified. Uploaded PDFs count as theses only if the person ticks that they are. Follow-up searches look for possible counterevidence but never declare a gap open or closed.
Evidence keeps exact character offsets and physical PDF page positions, and long theses are read as a head and tail sample so their final chapters are not missed.
The output is a single self-contained brief meant for the person's own AI assistant, built from the same request schema the command line uses.
